newsitem.title: USA: Ross ready to return soon to Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Ross ready to return soon to Mideast talks.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who is returning home from so far inconclusive Israeli-Palestinian talks, can return to the region quickly if required, Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Monday.
"Dennis will be prepared to go back in a few days, a week or so, as soon as his presence there will once again be very useful," Christopher told reporters.

Ross said earlier at a news conference in Jerusalem that he was leaving for Washington to report to Christopher after mediating for 15 days in the talks, which centre on a partial Israel pull-back from the West Bank town of Hebron.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Ross would return to the Middle East "at some point".
Christopher and Burns denied that the talks had broken down but said difficult issues continued to separate the negotiators.

"The progress that has been made has not been sufficient to conclude that issue because the issues are very difficult and require a good deal of precision," Christopher said before talks with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko.
"But the talks will continue, the United States role will continue" with U.S. diplomats in the region standing in for Ross, he said. "The negotiations are very detailed, very difficult," he added.

Burns said the United States thought Israel and the Palestinians had "made a lot of progress...We think that certainly Israel and the Palestinians have a greater sense of what the end result must be."

"We're confident of success in the end. But they're tough talks, and despite all the positive predictions in the Israeli press, including this morning, that the talks are about to succeed, they've still got a ways to go," he said.
